ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Triangle $ABC$ is isosceles, with $AB=AC$ and altitude $AM=11$. Suppose that there is a point $D$ on $\overline{AM}$ with $AD=10$ and $\angle BDC=3\angle BAC$. Then the perimeter of $\triangle ABC$ may be written in the form $a+\sqrt{b},$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Find $a+b$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, A is above, B and C are at the two ends of the base, AM is the vertical altitude from A to the base BC, and M is on BC. Point D is located on segment AM, and DB and DC are drawn in the figure; AM is labeled 11. Reasoning: Because AB=AC, in an isosceles triangle the altitude AM from vertex A to the base BC is also the perpendicular bisector of the base and the angle bisector of the vertex angle. Let BM=CM=x. Given AM=11 and AD=10, so DM=1. Let θ=∠BAM. From right triangle ABM, tan θ = BM/AM = x/11, therefore ∠BAC=2θ. Since D is also on the axis of symmetry AM, DM bisects ∠BDC. In right triangle BDM, tan(∠BDM)=BM/DM=x/1=x, so ∠BDC=2 arctan x. The condition ∠BDC=3∠BAC gives: 2 arctan x = 3(2θ)=6θ, therefore arctan x=3θ=3 arctan(x/11). Let t=x/11, then x=tan(3 arctan t). Using the formula tan(3u)=(3t-t^3)/(1-3t^2), obtain x=(3x/11 - x^3/1331)/(1 - 3x^2/121). Solving gives x=11/2. Thus BC=2x=11, and AB=AC=sqrt(11^2+x^2)=sqrt(121+121/4)=sqrt605/2. The perimeter of triangle ABC is 2AB+BC=sqrt605+11. Therefore a=11, b=605, and a+b=616.

method.method_draft: Let BM=CM=x, using the isosceles altitude shown to also be the perpendicular bisector. From the diagram/text, AM=11 and AD=10, so DM=1. The altitude AM bisects angle BAC, so if θ=∠BAM, then tan θ=x/11 and ∠BAC=2θ. Similarly, since D lies on the same perpendicular symmetry axis, ∠BDC is split in half by DM, and tan(∠BDM)=x/1=x, so ∠BDC=2 arctan x. The condition ∠BDC=3∠BAC becomes 2 arctan x=6θ, or arctan x=3 arctan(x/11). Apply tan(3u)=(3t-t^3)/(1-3t^2) with t=x/11, solve x=11/2. Then AB=AC=sqrt(11^2+x^2)=sqrt(121+121/4)=sqrt605/2 and BC=2x=11, giving perimeter 11+sqrt605, so a+b=616.

设θ=∠BAM。由直角三角形ABM，tan θ = BM/AM = x/11，因此∠BAC=2θ。

Reasoning: Because AB=AC, in an isosceles triangle the altitude AM from vertex A to the base BC is also the perpendicular bisector of the base and the angle bisector of the vertex angle. Let BM=CM=x. Given AM=11 and AD=10, so DM=1.

Let θ=∠BAM. From right triangle ABM, tan θ = BM/AM = x/11, therefore ∠BAC=2θ.

Since D is also on the axis of symmetry AM, DM bisects ∠BDC. In right triangle BDM, tan(∠BDM)=BM/DM=x/1=x, so ∠BDC=2 arctan x.

The condition ∠BDC=3∠BAC gives: 2 arctan x = 3(2θ)=6θ, therefore arctan x=3θ=3 arctan(x/11). Let t=x/11, then x=tan(3 arctan t). Using the formula tan(3u)=(3t-t^3)/(1-3t^2), obtain x=(3x/11 - x^3/1331)/(1 - 3x^2/121). Solving gives x=11/2.

Thus BC=2x=11, and AB=AC=sqrt(11^2+x^2)=sqrt(121+121/4)=sqrt605/2. The perimeter of triangle ABC is 2AB+BC=sqrt605+11. Therefore a=11, b=605, and a+b=616.
